note on sources: stichera (except stavrotheotokia and doxastochon of aposticha) are adapted from sergius by Ilya Galadza
ps140: 4, Podoben “As one valiant among the martyrs…”

Having finished the race and kept the Faith,* you were crowned with the wreath of martyrdom,* O Marcian and Martyrius,* unshakable pillars of the Church,* breasts putting forth the milk of truth,* lustrous pearls,  and beacons illumining creation** with the splendours of piety.

Having a single understanding among yourselves* and agreeing as one,  O godly twain,* you destroyed the division of Arius,* teaching all to worship the Son as consubstantial with the Father* and co-beginningless with the Spirit:* the Trinity in Unity,* the Unity in Trinity,** the one Godhead indivisible in three Hypostases.

You showed yourselves to be like-minded followers,* emulators and zealots of the sacred preacher Paul,* and with the outpouring of your blood* you drowned the enemy,* drying up the torrent of grievous heresies* and revealing yourselves to be rivers of piety,* watering the Church of Christ,** O Marcian and Martyrius.

As disciples and followers of the preacher* and confessor of the consubstantial Trinity,* you were persecuted with him,  O blessed ones,* preferring death by the sword to blasphemous heresy.* Wherefore, adorned by God with crowns of martyrdom,* and having received boldness before Him,* pray, that those who honour your memory** be delivered from misfortunes.
stavrotheotokion: The unblemished ewe-lamb and Mistress,* beholding her Lamb upon the Cross, bereft of form and beauty,* said, lamenting: Woe is me!* Where has Your beauty set, O You who are most sweet?* Where is Your comeliness?* Where is the radiant grace of Your image,* O my Son most beloved?
aposticha: Marcian and Martyrius* conquered heresies with the shield of faith,* enlightening the world with the light of orthodoxy!* They are champions of the Trinity and spiritual beacons of the Church!* Obedient to Paul, the equal of the apostles,* they cast down the division of Arius and Nestorius,* refuting also the mingling of Sabellius and Severus.* They theologized about the Unity in Trinity,* the God Who was incarnate of the Virgin!* The most blessed ones preached to all one Christ in two natures!* Now that they have received crowns of victory from heaven,* these heralds of God pray for great mercy for our souls!
stavrotheotokion_aposticha: A sword pierced your soul, O most pure one, when you beheld your Son upon the Cross, and you cried out: "Do not make me childless, O my Son and my God, You who preserved me a Virgin even after childbirth!"
